newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKBROKERS ASS'N ACCUSES GOVMT OF COVERUP.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKBROKERS ASS'N ACCUSES GOVMT OF COVERUP.

text.p: The Greek stockbrokers association accused the government of attempting to cover-up a scandal which has rocked the bourse and stopped almost all trade for the past three working days.

"We condemn this attempt by the government which ... aims, even if unintentionally, at covering up possible ... illegal actions," the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA) said in a statement.

"We have decided to remain on the sidelines of this attempted cover-up, believing that the (government's) decision will lead the market to a deadend with tragic repercussions for investors," it added.
In its clearest challenge to the government since the bourse crisis erupted last week, SMEHA also slammed the government for trying to force trade to resume at the bourse on Tuesday.
State banks ordered their subsidiary brokerages to go to the bourse and, to resounding boos and insults from colleagues, they executed a handful of trades.
The bourse has been effectively closed since last Friday, after one brokerage, Delta Securities, defaulted on 2.6 billion drachmas in settlement payments with the bourse clearing house.
Delta's assets and accounts have been frozen and its three senior officials charged with "large-scale and repeated fraud", which if convicted carries a maximum 15-year sentence.

With several brokerages said to have been counter-parties to trades with Delta, and the Greek media raising the issue of possible share price manipulation, many brokers were questioning the reason behind the decision to resume trading before the mess over cash settlement was investigated fully.
Several brokers said that if trade resumed, open positions, which could help determine the extent of the Delta fraud, could be closed, making discovery difficult.
